If D > 0, you get two real roots via x = (-b ± √D) / (2a). If D = 0, one real double root exists. If D < 0, the roots are complex. This systematic approach clarifies each step.

To find stationary points, first differentiate f(x) to get f'(x). Then, set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points.
